page: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for compute-heavy and graphics-intensive workloads. It features 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6448H processor operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 375.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.72 GB per core. For acceleration, it integrates two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 2200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier performance in LLM inference tasks. For a small 135M model, the instance achieves 13643.47 tokens per second for prompt processing and 348.06 tokens per second for text generation. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing reaches 6275.36 tokens per second, and text generation reaches 141.42 tokens per second. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 62892.75 and a Passmark CPU score of 64768.69. Memory bandwidth is also highly capable, with read-only small block cached bandwidth measured at 4985.78 GB/sec.

While the instance delivers exceptional parallel processing capabilities via its dual NVIDIA L40S GPUs and high-capacity memory, certain tradeoffs exist. The CPU allocation is shared, and single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2209.29. Additionally, large-block memory write bandwidth is average at 88.2 GB/sec compared to its strong read performance. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of GPU VRAM and system memory relative to the 32 vCPUs makes this instance a resource-dense option for workloads that can fully utilize GPU acceleration without requiring dedicated CPU cores.

This server configuration is highly suited for large language model inference, machine learning training, and high-performance data science jobs. The combination of 2200 GB NVMe storage and strong database benchmarks, such as 70.17 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, also makes it viable for memory-intensive database operations and real-time analytics.
